title: AMemOps: Evaluating Memory Updates in Long Audio Streams
abstract: arXiv:2610.18652v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Audio memory must recognise recurring sources across acoustic changes while keeping their attributes up to date. Overall accuracy does not reveal how these demands interact. We introduce Audio Memory Operations (AMemOps), a benchmark for latest-attribute retrieval, preservation of unchanged attributes and absent-source rejection in long audio streams. Paired controls vary recordings, training identities and earlier events to examine their effects on updating. Training on other recordings of the test instruments increases a reference delta-rule memory's update advantage over matched attention by 13.4 percentage points. At retrieval delays of 120\,s, matched histories separate benefits of consistent repetition from costs of conflicting earlier values, while additive-memory controls identify benefits of erasure.

translated_title: AMemOps：评估长音频流中的记忆更新
translated_abstract: 音频记忆必须在声学变化中识别反复出现的声源，同时保持其属性的最新状态。总体准确率无法揭示这些需求之间是如何相互作用的。我们提出了音频记忆操作（AMemOps），这是一个针对长音频流中最新属性检索、未变属性保持和缺席声源拒绝的基准测试。通过配对对照实验改变录音、训练身份和早期事件，以检验它们对更新的影响。在测试乐器的其他录音上进行训练，使参考的增量规则记忆相对于匹配的注意力机制的更新优势提高了13.4个百分点。在120秒的检索延迟下，匹配的历史记录能够将一致重复带来的收益与冲突早期值带来的代价区分开来，而加性记忆对照实验则识别出擦除机制的优势。
tldr: 该论文提出了AMemOps基准，用于评估长音频流中音频记忆的属性更新能力，并发现在相关录音上训练可使增量规则记忆相对注意力机制的更新优势提升13.4个百分点。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AMemOps, a benchmark for evaluating audio memory updates in long audio streams, showing that training on related recordings boosts a delta-rule memory's update advantage over matched attention by 13.4 percentage points.
